headline_numbers.note_on_count: Official index lists 94 numbered acts; BAA 93 and 94 appear to be the same SGADA-expansion act listed twice.

phases_of_lawmaking.pattern: Flag, emblem, hymn, seal; annual budgets; the first three priority codes (Administrative, Civil Service, Education). The parliament was literally building the state's symbols and machinery before legislating policy.

Six hospital acts passed in one week of June 2022 (the outgoing first BTA's final sprint); then the second BTA delivered the Electoral Code, Local Governance Code, and created nine new municipalities - eight of them in the Special Geographic Area in a single day (Aug 17, 2023).

Mujahideen financial assistance, martyr memorials (Salamat Hashim, Camp Abubakar), IDP rights, Indigenous Peoples rights, plus a second hospital wave (5 acts on Dec 12, 2024 alone) and the first districting law (BAA 58).

Dominated by the fallout of two shocks: the SC's exclusion of Sulu from BARMM and the SC voiding of districting law BAA 58. Result: BAA 77, then BAA 86 (apportionment), BAA 87-88 (electoral code amendments), all racing the Sept 14, 2026 election date - alongside a third hospital wave and the long-delayed Labor Code (BAA 82).

priority_codes.mandated_by: Bangsamoro Organic Law (RA 11054) requires the BTA to enact seven priority codes during transition.

codes.status: PENDING - Bill 286 filed 2024, still unenacted as of Aug 2026; the last unfinished priority code

most_amended.BAA 13 (Administrative Code): amended by BAA 37, 93/94; multiple pending amendment bills (409, 447, 474)
most_amended.BAA 58 (Districting): amended by BAA 77, then effectively replaced by BAA 86 after SC rulings

thematic_findings: Hospitals are the single biggest BAA category (18 acts: [21, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 66, 67, 68, 69, 73, 74, 76, 78, 79, 80, 83]). Health infrastructure - creating, upgrading, renaming hospitals - is the BTA's most reliable legislative output, and hospital acts cluster at session endings (Jun 2022, Dec 2024, Aug 2025), suggesting they serve as consensus 'deliverables'.

Budget/finance measures are second (20 acts): 7 annual GAAs (FY2020-FY2026), 4+ supplementals, and repeated validity-extension acts - the latter indicating chronic under-disbursement of appropriated funds in the early years.

Municipality creation (15 acts) is concentrated in the Special Geographic Area - the 63 North Cotabato barangays that voted to join BARMM - converting plebiscite promises into LGU structures (8 municipalities in one day in 2023).

Peace-process legacy is written directly into statute: mujahideen assistance (57), martyr memorial sites (60, 61), Camp Abubakar eco-park, transitional justice commission (89) - laws that institutionalize the MILF-government peace agreement's memory and obligations.
The Revenue Code is the conspicuous gap: the only Organic Law priority code still unenacted as the transition ends, leaving BARMM fiscally dependent on the national block grant.
Election-related lawmaking shows external-shock reactivity: 5 of the last 10 BAAs respond directly to Supreme Court rulings (Sulu exclusion, districting unconstitutionality).
